summary: Lights have marked Conneaut Harbor on Lake Erie since 1835; the breakwater light of 1936 was automated in 1972 and is now privately owned.

structures.note: Commissioned 1 April 1936 at a cost of $70,000 (LighthouseFriends). 60 ft base to lantern (USLHS).
Light placed in commission 15 Sept 1920; blasted from its footing in 1934-1936 (LighthouseFriends)
Breakwater light placed October 1906; about 31.5 ft tall (LighthouseFriends)

access.note: Privately owned; stands on a breakwater that is not connected to land. Archive: not open to the public. LighthouseFriends: some people wade or swim out.

corrections.why: The standing tower was commissioned on 1 April 1936 (LighthouseFriends; archive). The record's 1905 date and 12.0 m height fit neither the wooden breakwater light of 1906 (about 31.5 ft, LighthouseFriends) nor the 60-ft steel tower of 1936 (archive).

corrections.proposed: alternating red and white flashes, 5 s period
corrections.why: LighthouseFriends describes the current tower's characteristic as alternating red and white flashes with a five-second period. The record's 'Fl R 10s' is not supported by the sources read. Proposed for human review only.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Board's 1894 report says the 1835 light stood on the outer end of the west pier; LighthouseFriends says it stood on the eastern pier. The sources do not settle it, so both are given in the story.

notes_for_editor: Conflicts left in the story: (1) the 1835 light stood on the outer end of the west pier (Board, 1894) or atop the eastern pier (LighthouseFriends); (2) the pierhead beacon date, 1875 (LighthouseFriends) or the west-pier move in 1885 (Board); (3) Edward Pfister's start: head keeper 1894 (LighthouseFriends) or 1906 (archive); the 1894 date may refer to the older harbour lights, but no source says so; (4) the 1920 light's start of restoration work: 'resumed in June, 1919' (Commissioner 1919) or 'June 9, 1920' (Commissioner 1920); (5) the keeper's dwelling: 1872 (LighthouseFriends) or 1873 (archive); (6) the 1906 breakwater light is a fixed white light (LighthouseFriends), while the 1915 Bulletin lists a 'group flashing white' Conneaut West Breakwater light; these may be different lights; (7) the 1936 tower's characteristic: the record's 'Fl R 10s' (range 10.4 nm) is not supported by the sources read, and LighthouseFriends describes alternating red and white flashes with a five-second period; the correction is proposed, not applied; (8) the Commissioner's 1921 report gives the total appropriation as $90,100, while LighthouseFriends gives a total cost of $89,667 for the lighthouse and related aids; (9) the archive's 'Private Aid: No' sits alongside LighthouseFriends' private ownership, which is not a conflict (the light is a federal aid on private property); (10) LighthouseFriends says grounds are open and the tower closed, while the archive says not open to the public; the story follows the archive and says that some people wade or swim out. Ownership names of the 2011 private buyers are left out; the 2008 buyer is named in his published public role. The breakwater is leased from the Army Corps of Engineers. The NRHP nomination text (ID 92000243) is not digitised in the cache, so the 1992 listing rests on LighthouseFriends. The Bulletin index entry for the 1920s efficiency flag was not used. The Board volumes' scan pages are confirmed by the corpus grep (page labels printed in the snippets); the 1895 and 1899 volume pages were confirmed by the archive's page index; the 1896-97 page for 408 was confirmed by the archive search. The 1893 Board page 200 is in the fiscal-1893 report by its text ('until the close of navigation, 1892'). The 1915 Commissioner report p. 84 is cited for the estimate and the 3 March 1915 authorisation. A Chronicling America search for Pfister and Conneaut Harbor (Ohio, 1906-1937) returned no hits, so no newspaper evidence is used.
